definitions.explanation: Describes eggs (or occasionally other foods) that have been boiled until the yolk and white are completely set and firm.

examples.japanese: {固|かた}ゆで{卵|たまご}を{作|つく}った。
{固|かた}ゆでにするには{十二分|じゅうにふん}ほど{茹|ゆ}でる。
examples.english: Boil for about twelve minutes to make them hard-boiled.

examples.japanese: サラダには{半熟|はんじゅく}より{固|かた}ゆでの{方|ほう}が{崩|くず}れなくて{使|つか}いやすい。
examples.english: Hard-boiled eggs are easier to use in salads than soft-boiled ones since they don't fall apart.

notes:
Also written as {固茹|かたゆ}で. A cooking term composed of {固|かた} (hard, firm) and {茹|ゆ}で (boiling). Almost always used in reference to eggs. Can function as a noun ({固|かた}ゆで{卵|たまご}) or as a descriptive modifier ({固|かた}ゆでにする).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {固|かた}ゆで{卵|たまご}: hard-boiled egg
- {固|かた}ゆでにする: to hard-boil
- {固|かた}ゆでの{卵|たまご}: hard-boiled egg

SIMILAR WORDS:
- {半熟|はんじゅく}: soft-boiled, half-cooked — the opposite, with a runny yolk
- {温泉卵|おんせんたまご}: hot spring egg — egg with set white and runny yolk
- {茹|ゆ}で{卵|たまご}: boiled egg — general term, regardless of doneness
